six_problem_months_note: Verified against live ALFRED and against the BLS news-release archive. The previously selected dates (2006-05-08, 2012-12-12, 2013-05-06, 2020-05-11, 2024-01-10, 2024-08-21) are off-cycle seasonal-factor/benchmark revisions.

headline.estimand: Friday NFP sessions vs Friday non-NFP sessions (weekday held fixed)
headline.significance_flip_note: The claimed 'significant -> not significant' flip does NOT hold, under either estimand. Friday-restricted: 1.189x p=0.0209. Old mixed-weekday spec on correct dates: 1.177x p=0.0257. Codex v2 predicted 1.1779/0.02488 for the mixed spec; the small delta is the control-group leak fix found in round 2. The flip was an artifact of six wrong event dates.

findings_addressed.4: fail-closed completed. check_calendar_is_complete now validates the RAW feed as well as the accessor's selection: malformed selection (duplicate month, month/date absent from raw), non-earliest selection, same-month pair too close to disambiguate, unreviewed or re-shaped multi-entry month, month present in raw but missing from selection, requested-window coverage, gaps inside the observed span, and a KNOWN_MISSING_MONTHS claim contradicted by the raw feed. Event->session mapping asserts one-to-one (unmapped in-sample release raises; two releases colliding on one session raises); window-buffer exclusions are recorded, not silent.
findings_addressed.5: Friday baseline estimand repaired by restricting the event group to Friday releases (237), so weekday is held fixed on both sides. weekday-matched controls rejected because the non-Friday cells are Mon 6 / Tue 2 / Wed 1 / Thu 7 -- too thin for a stable weighted average. Disclosed: the restriction is NOT neutral (excluded events are 16.3% quieter, so it raises the ratio), and the result is conditional on Friday. IMPORTANT: this defect predates the date correction -- the proxy run was already 239/254 Friday, not 254/254 as originally claimed.
findings_addressed.6: directional overreach removed. 'insignificant across all tests' is gone; every significance statement names its own test. Welch vs all days does not reject (p=0.112) while the one-sided Mann-Whitney does (p=0.0019), and the artifact says so instead of collapsing them. The VIX-regime comparison is stated as the largest number in the study, explicitly NOT as a formally-tested ranking or a causal claim.
findings_addressed.7: atomic writes: main results and audit use tempfile + fsync + os.replace. builder dry-run now writes nothing at all (verified by sha256 + mtime); recording is opt-in via --record-plan or --apply.
findings_addressed.8: archive JSON carries superseded=true, do_not_cite=true, superseded_by, retraction_reason, impact_on_published_numbers and the proxy date source in the object itself, so it is identifiable as retracted without its filename or README.

corrections_rebuilt.void_reason: The 18-item list was built against the contaminated rerun and contained a DIRECTIONAL reversal: it rewrote 'reaches significance' into 'p=0.057, just misses'. The article was right the first time. Applying it would have published a retraction of a correct finding.

self_found_defects: control group retained the window-excluded NFP session 2005-01-07 (found before Codex round 1 reported it independently)
the claim 'every proxy NFP was a Friday' was false (239/254); found by checking my own README claim against the archive
window-coverage hole: anchoring the completeness span on min..max(selected) cannot detect a truncated feed
notes: merge_allowed stays false until a Codex round returns PASS on the exact bytes it read. This file is not part of the certified claim surface (*.py + README.md + *_results.json), so it is written and updated around the review rounds by design. One correction worth recording against myself: in round 3 I removed a working same-month gap gate, claiming the real feed 'straddled' its threshold. It did not -- the condition was `gap < 3` and the real minimum is exactly 3, which passes. I had changed `<` to `<=` first and then deleted the gate on the strength of my own mistake. Codex caught it; the gate is restored at `< 3` and the allowlist now pins each reviewed month's full raw entry set rather than just its name.
